items.title: Manny Albam interviewed by Monk Rowe, Tarrytown, New York, October 31, 1998
items.q: Monk Rowe is identified as the interviewer and director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive who conducted the interview. No personal or professional relationship beyond the interview context is described.

ctx.x: Manny Albam is one of America’s most prolific and innovative composers in jazz, classical and film music. He was born in 1922 in the Dominican Republic and grew up in New York City. He worked as a saxophonist with numerous big bands in the 40s and devoted himself to full time writing in 1951. Manny’s scores have been played by a long list of jazz luminaries including Gerry Mulligan, Count Basie, Carmen McRae and Dizzy Gillespie. His original compositions include chamber music and large scale pieces for studio…
Manny was interviewed in Tarrytown, New York on October 31, 1998, by Monk Rowe, director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.

My name is Monk Rowe. We are filming for the Hamilton College Jazz Archive in Tarrytown, New York, and I’m very pleased to have composer and arranger Manny Albam with me today. I’m going to pick up a thought you just had before the cameras were rolling, and that is retirement has been a busier time than ever for you.
